Devil's Advocate · four attacks

① Bull: CAPE is overstated (Siegel)Softening

Even at a fair CAPE=25, 40→25 is still a de-rating; to overturn requires CAPE permanently at 40 AND nominal EPS growth ≥8.3%/yr (several times the 1.5% historical trend).

② Bear: tail risk at Fragility 0.92 is understatedRaise tail

Triggers can flip from dormant to ignited within weeks; basis 18:1, Fed/IMF flag fragility. Opposite direction — raise the tail-risk alert.

③ Method: does it hold without the n=7 backtestHolds

The long-term conclusion rests on T1 valuation + T2 accounting identity, not the backtest; the backtest was only "illustrative." Removing it is actually cleaner.

Survival checkDirection survives

After all four attacks, "valuation direction = down" survives. Only "how deep, when" can be shaken — and those were never questions valuation should answer.
